what: What did each Lunenburg town employee earn in 2001?
why: `report-gross-wages` holds per-employee earnings from the 2010 report (calendar wages) and FY2011-FY2025 (fiscal). The 2001 annual town report prints no wage list: its Textract text was searched for wages, gross, earnings, salary, payroll, compensation and employee on every page with text (92 of 94) and returned only prose in department reports (p17, p19, p25, p28, p38), department-level payroll lines in the appropriations schedule (p55-60) and the omnibus budget (p81-82), and the receipts line EARNINGS ON INVESTMENTS (p53) -- no list by employee (sources/data/report-tables/2001/). — closes: the Town's calendar-2001 payroll register (W-2 totals by employee) from the Treasurer's office.

what: What were the town's non-union salary grades and step rates in 2001?
why: `salary-schedule` and `report-classification-plan` read Schedule A from the 2010 report and FY2011 onward. The 2001 annual town report prints neither: its text was searched for salary schedule, classification plan, step and grade-with-a-dollar-figure on every page with text (92 of 94) and returned nothing (sources/data/report-tables/2001/). — closes: the Personnel Bylaw Schedule A (salary schedule and classification plan) in force for FY2002, from the Town Clerk or the Personnel Committee.

what: How many weighing and measuring devices did the Sealer test in 2001, and what did sealing bring in by device?
why: `report-weights-measures` holds the Sealer's device counts and fees from the 2010 report. The 2001 annual town report prints no Inspector of Weights & Measures report: its text was searched for weights, sealer and sealing and returned only the appointment (p8), the receipts line SEALING FEES $941.00 (p53), the appropriation line (p56) and the omnibus line Sealer of Wgts & Meas (p81) (sources/data/report-tables/2001/). — closes: the Sealer of Weights and Measures' 2001 annual report to the Division of Standards.

what: What did each item of Lunenburg's FY2002 capital plan cost?
why: `capital-plans` holds item-by-item costs. The 2001 annual town report prints the FY2002 plan only as three article totals with the items listed in prose and no amount per item: Articles 38 ($175,000, capital expenditure), 39 ($193,000, capital improvements) and 40 ($24,210, capital maintenance), all VOTED UNANIMOUSLY (p86), and the Capital Planning Committee's report names the items without costs (p12) (sources/data/report-tables/2001/). — closes: the Capital Planning Committee's FY2002 Capital Plan as presented to the 5/12/2001 Annual Town Meeting.

what: How much of Lunenburg's debt at 30 June 2001 sat inside the debt limit, and how much outside it?
why: `outstanding-debt` reads this from the five-year outstanding-debt summary the FY2011-FY2025 reports print. The 2001 annual town report prints its bonded indebtedness issue by issue (PDF page 69) and a repayment schedule (p70) whose principal lines carry an exempt share for two issues (`PRINCIPAL (82% EXEMPT)`, `PRINCIPAL (69% EXEMPT)`) but no summary by purpose and no debt-limit split: its text was searched for debt limit, outstanding debt and long-term indebtedness and returned nothing. — closes: the Town's FY2001 Statement of Indebtedness as filed with the Division of Local Services.
